fields.meta_description: Build a JHA form template your crew fills in on a phone, with job steps, hazards, controls ranked by type, and signatures in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a JHA Form Template Crews Sign Before Work
fields.hero_description: Build a JHA form template that lists each job step with its hazards and controls and gets crew signatures before work starts.
fields.features_heading: What the Crew Checks Before the Job Starts
fields.features_subheading: A paper JHA gets read once and filed. Build the form with Emergent, and the next crew opens the same steps, hazards, and signatures.
fields.feature_1:
Steps listed in the order the job runs

Each job step gets its own row, in the order the worker does it. Under every step, the form lists what can go wrong, how badly someone could be hurt, and the controls set for it.
fields.feature_2:
Controls tagged engineering, admin, or PPE

Every control carries a type: engineering, administrative, or PPE. A hazard whose only control is PPE gets a flag and goes to the safety manager before the crew starts work.
fields.feature_3:
Crew signatures on one phone

Each worker reads the steps and signs on the crew lead's phone or on their own. The app records who signed and at what time, and a job still missing a signature shows as not ready.
fields.feature_4:
A new version asks for new signatures

Change a step or a control, and the app saves the JHA as a new version and asks every worker on that job to sign it again. The old version and its signatures stay on file beside it.
fields.feature_5:
A review when an injury names the job

An injury or near-miss report that names a job marks that job's JHA for review and emails the safety lead. The JHA stays marked until someone signs off on the revised version.
fields.feature_6:
Every JHA in a database you own

Keep every JHA, signature, and revision in a database you own. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the form next to the rest of your safety program.

faq_plan.q: What is a jha form template?
How do I create a jha form template?

plan.angle: The top 10 for jha form template is downloadable PDF, Word and Excel sheets plus OSHA's own booklet: a grid for job steps, hazards and controls that someone fills in once and files. This page builds the JHA form as an app a crew opens on a phone at the job: steps listed in order, each hazard with its controls tagged by type, a flag when a hazard leans on PPE alone, crew signatures before work starts, and a review the moment an injury report names the job. The how-to and FAQ add what the printables skip: which jobs to analyze first, how to break a job into steps, and when a JHA needs a second look.
tab_stories: Thornbeck Roofing crew lead Jorund Pell opens the tear-off JHA on his phone, walks its 5 steps with the crew, and all 4 crew members sign before tear-off starts.

At Brisbourne Castings the only control on a dropped 15-pound casting is steel-toe boots, so the app flags it as PPE only and sends it to safety manager Isaura Velloway, who adds a table beside the grinder.
An injury report at Gorsedge Freight names the pallet restack job, so its JHA moves to Under review and safety lead Stellan Quaye gets an email with step 3 marked.
Larkmoor Facilities revises its boiler room JHA, 9 of 12 technicians have signed the new version, and the 3 still unsigned get an email each morning until they sign.

claims_to_source: OSHA defines a job hazard analysis as a technique that focuses on job tasks to identify hazards before they occur
OSHA gives priority to jobs that could cause severe or disabling injury even with no accident history
OSHA says to watch the employee perform the job and list each step as the worker takes it
OSHA says involving employees helps minimize oversights
OSHA ranks engineering controls as the most effective, then administrative controls when engineering controls are not feasible
OSHA accepts PPE as a control when engineering controls are not feasible or do not totally eliminate the hazard
OSHA says it is particularly important to review the JHA if an illness or injury occurs on a specific job
OSHA says to train all employees affected by the changes any time a JHA is revised
